lines.trans: Did I not tell you never to accept personal deliveries at the office?!
This one came addressed to you, Producer—it looks like Cindy's fan club.
Hey, get that away! Who knows if there is a dead mouse or something inside—do not open it!
Wait—the card says they love you! Did you not know? Cindy uploaded a post!
It reads: During my honey-sweet break, together with always warm-hearted Producer Tak Ye-jin!
Well of course, I have always had an affectionate disposition—she simply spoke the truth!
Whoa hey, does this post really have five thousand six hundred likes?
That means people like Cindy—not that they like you, Producer.
Korea's prettiest producer! Oh stop it—these kids clearly saw me in real life!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.
Did you hear about this personal?
I was busy today because of personal.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Used as noun (글).

examples.trans: Wait—the card says they love you! Did you not know? Cindy uploaded a post!

examples.text: 너네 이제 이상한 글 쓰면 내가 다 지워버릴 거야!
examples.trans: From now on, the moment any of you write nasty posts, I am deleting every single one!

meanings.note: Used as noun (꿀).

examples.text: 꿀 같은 휴식 중 늘 다정한 탁예진 피디님과 함께!
examples.trans: It reads: During my honey-sweet break, together with always warm-hearted Producer Tak Ye-jin!
This point about honey is really important.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.text: 걱정은 하지, 늘. 근데 왜 백승찬을 집에 자꾸 들이냐?
examples.trans: I always worry. Still, why do you keep letting Baek Seung-chan into the house?

examples.text: 늘 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (always), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Used as adnominal (다정한).

examples.text: 꿀 같은 휴식 중 늘 다정한 탁예진 피디님과 함께!
examples.trans: It reads: During my honey-sweet break, together with always warm-hearted Producer Tak Ye-jin!

examples.text: 그렇지, 내가 늘 다정한 성품이지! 할 말 했어!
examples.trans: Well of course, I have always had an affectionate disposition—she simply spoke the truth!

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Have you lost your mind? You are driving me crazy—no way!
This expression comes from 'driving me nuts'.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Used as noun + locative (사무실에서).

examples.text: 나 회사 가서 자려고. 숙직실 가서 자도 되고 사무실에서 자도 되고.
examples.trans: I am going to sleep at the station—I can sleep in the night-duty room or in the office.
This point about in the office is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun + copula + -지 (성품이지!).

examples.text: 그렇지, 내가 늘 다정한 성품이지! 할 말 했어!
examples.trans: Well of course, I have always had an affectionate disposition—she simply spoke the truth!
This point about have that character is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (실물을).

examples.text: 대한민국 최고 얼짱 피디! 미치겠다 진짜, 얘들이 내 실물을 봤네 봤어!
examples.trans: Korea's prettiest producer! Oh stop it—these kids clearly saw me in real life!
This point about real-life looks is really important.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close
dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun (얼짱).

examples.text: 대한민국 최고 얼짱 피디! 미치겠다 진짜, 얘들이 내 실물을 봤네 봤어!
examples.trans: Korea's prettiest producer! Oh stop it—these kids clearly saw me in real life!
This point about best-looking is really important.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

examples.text: 너 방금 뭐라고? 내가 널 어떻게 이 자리까지 올렸는데!
examples.trans: What did you just say? Do you know how hard I worked to raise you to this position!

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 올리다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (raised, brought up).

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.
Test
Test2

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Used as social-media noun + subject (좋아요가).

examples.trans: Whoa hey, does this post really have five thousand six hundred likes?
This point about 'likes' is really important.

meanings.en: to be dying of (hyperbolic emphasis in -아/어 죽겠다)

examples.trans: I'm starving to death.
It's so hot I feel like I'm going to die.

meanings.note: Bound noun placed after another noun to indicate an ongoing activity or time period, usually followed by 에 (중에). RR: jung.

examples.trans: I am in a meeting right now.
Please do not make phone calls during class.

meanings.note: Used as noun (쥐).

examples.text: 야 치워 치워! 이거 죽은 쥐 이런 거 들었는지도 몰라, 하지 마!
examples.trans: Hey, get that away! Who knows if there is a dead mouse or something inside—do not open it!
This point about mouse, rat is really important.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
Did you hear about this the best!?
I was busy today because of the best!.

meanings.note: Used as casual question (치워?).

examples.text: 야, 뭘 깨끗한데 계속 치워? 내 차보다 훨씬 깨끗하다.
examples.trans: Hey, why do you keep tidying up when it is already clean? It is way cleaner than my car.
Let us do that (cleaning up) right away.
Did you hear about this parcel delivery?
I was busy today because of parcel delivery.

meanings.note: Used as noun + locative (팬클럽에서).

examples.text: 지금 신디 팬클럽에서 신디의 사고에 피디님의 고의성이 있다 없다 투표 들어갔거든요.
examples.trans: Right now Cindy's fan club has opened a poll on whether your role in Cindy's accident was intentional or not.
This point about in the fan club is really important.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 여기서 선택을 못 받아서 낙오되신 분들은 신입 피디와 함께 갑니다.
examples.trans: Anyone not chosen here and left behind will travel with our rookie producer.

examples.text: 함께 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (together), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 덕분에 간만에 주어진 휴식이랄까, 오랜만에 세 시간 이상 푹 잤어요.
examples.trans: Thanks to this, it feels like my first real break in ages—for the first time in forever I slept soundly for over three hours.
Here the word for 'call it a break' is key.
